Data Is Not an Advantage. But Data-Enabled Speed Is.  
Data network effects aren’t real.
 Data is almost never a moat.

But data systems can be powerful advantages. 

Here’s how I think about it.

Note: I have a full podcast episode on this. Link below.

Point 1: Data is rarely a moat, but it is a powerful operating tool.

Data is key to operating performance. 
 But not a moat. 

Proprietary data that is a scarce resource is an exception to this.

Point 2: Decision speed is where data pays off first
 Having a great data dashboard is like playing chess where you get to move twice for every time your rival moves once.

Point 3: Rate of learning and adaptation are the real prize.

An organization that can adapt to data is powerful.
 It starts with personalization and quick reactions to what customers do.

***Takeaways for Managers:

Takeaway 1: Measure how long your team takes from idea to decision, then set a target to cut it.

Takeaway 2: Give one agile team a ready to use data product, not raw data lake access.

fullText:
Impressive paper from Stanford on harness evolution for robotics.

They improve frozen robot policies from 9.7% to 43.3% success on unseen scenes without changing a single weight.

The gain comes from the harness.

RoboArchitect gives a coding model the robot's rollouts. The coding model diagnoses failures and rewrites the control code around the frozen policy. That code decides when to call the policy, when to use vision tools and when to command the arm directly.

The harness is optimized on one set of episodes and tested on held-out scenes and tasks. Success on unseen tasks rises from 12.7% to 40.2%.

The largest gains appear where the benchmark is far from the policy's training data. Inside an evolved harness, a general-purpose policy often beats the finetuned version of the same policy.

The search also produced control routines such as lifting a jammed arm clear, and it added a persistent memory that stores values like effective grasp depths.
